name: VoiceAssistant-Eval
description: VoiceAssistant-Eval is a comprehensive benchmark designed to assess AI assistants across listening, speaking, and viewing. It comprises 10,497 curated examples spanning 13 task categories, including natural sounds, music, and spoken dialogue for listening; multi-turn dialogue, role-play imitation, and various scenarios for speaking; and highly heterogeneous images for viewing. The benchmark addresses four key weaknesses in existing benchmarks: lack of voice personalization evaluation, limited focus on hands-free interaction, neglect of various audio contexts in daily life, and insufficient multi-modal (vision+audio) integration assessment.
creator: Ke Wang, Houxing Ren, Zimu Lu, Mingjie Zhan, Hongsheng Li (CUHK MMLab, SenseTime Research, CPII under InnoHK)
citeAs: Wang, K., Ren, H., Lu, Z., Zhan, M., & Li, H. (2025). VoiceAssistant-Eval: Benchmarking AI Assistants Across Listening, Speaking, and Viewing. arXiv:2509.22651.
rai:dataCollection: Data was collected from 47 source datasets spanning audio and visual modalities. For the Listening subset, source data was extracted from 23 audio understanding datasets covering speech, sound, music, and general audio. For the Speaking subset, data came from 22 datasets including 11 text datasets and 11 audio datasets, with role-play data from RoleBench. For the Viewing subset, MMMU was used as the source dataset spanning 30 disciplines and 30 image formats. Text instructions were converted to audio using TTS models. For role-play, 100 distinct roles were selected and three representative audio clips per role were collected.
rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Web Scraping, Manual Human Curator
rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Approximately 10% of candidates were removed during the curation process due to missing or broken audio or images, as well as instances with ill-posed questions or incorrect answers.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Data was extracted from 47 source datasets including: MMMU, VocalBench, AlpacaEval, MMSU, RoleBench, AdvBench, AIR-Bench, MEAD, BeaverTails-Eval, MT-Bench-101, VCTK, IFEval, MusicCaps, CommonVoice, SD-Eval, Nsynth, BIG-Bench Hard, Clotho, SLURP, VoiceBench, MTG-Jamendo, JL Corpus, MELD, AudioCaps, AudioGrounding, CoVoST 2, LibriSpeech, VocalSound, VoxCeleb1, MUSIA-AVQA, FoR, SpeechInstructBench, IEMOCAP, FollowBench, SpokenWOZ, TUT2017, AVQA, CommonsenseQA, GSM8K, STORAL, Clotho-AQA, FMA, CochlScene, Fisher, MT Bench, RAVDESS, MyST.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Text instructions were converted to audio using three TTS models (F5-TTS, ChatTTS, Dia-1.6B). Text preprocessing included: replacing image reference tokens with descriptive phrases, rewriting text using Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct for TTS suitability (converting numbers, math expressions, and multiple-choice options to spoken form). Speech was synthesized and evaluated with UTMOS Strong, regenerated until score surpassed 3.8. Synthesized audio was transcribed with Whisper-Large-v3 and the sample with the lowest word error rate was retained. In total, 13,471 high-quality speech audio files were synthesized.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: A four-stage curation process was applied: (1) Deduplication using lexical overlap and Levenshtein distance to flag potential duplicates, which were manually reviewed and removed, resulting in 15,359 samples; (2) Validation to exclude incomplete or unsuitable instances including entries with corrupted images, silent audio, ill-posed prompts, and demonstrably incorrect answers (approximately 10% discarded); (3) Categorization assigning remaining problems to 13 predefined task categories based on source metadata; (4) Sampling to balance the ratio of different tasks, resulting in 10,497 high-quality samples.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: A triadic evaluation system was used: (1) Content quality assessed using gpt-oss-20b with thirteen task-specific evaluator prompts comparing model outputs to reference answers; (2) Speech quality measured using UTMOS (providing fluency and naturalness scores); (3) Consistency between text and speech modalities computed using a modified Word Error Rate (WER) after transcribing speech outputs with Whisper-Large-v3. For role-play tasks, Wespeaker was used to calculate speaker similarity between model-generated speech and reference role audio. For emotion tasks, emotion2vec was used to get emotion probabilities. The final score for each task is calculated by multiplying the three individual scores.
rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: A lightweight web-based curation tool was built for manual quality review. Curators reviewed each item on a single screen with inline players and viewers, transcripts, and multiple-choice options, assigning Good or Bad verdicts with optional notes.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Human evaluation validation was conducted on 10% of Qwen2.5-Omni-7B's responses (1,050 examples) across all 13 tasks. Pearson correlation coefficients between automated (gpt-oss-20b) and human evaluations ranged from 0.73 to 1.00 (overall 0.92). Agreement rates were uniformly high (often above 90%), with an overall agreement rate of 96.1%. Evaluation stability was assessed by repeating scoring 10 times on 10% of responses, showing low variance (standard deviations mostly below 3). Statistical significance testing was performed using paired two-sided t-tests with Bonferroni correction.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: gpt-oss-20b (content quality evaluation), UTMOS Strong / UTMOS (speech quality evaluation), Whisper-Large-v3 (speech transcription for WER computation), emotion2vec (emotion probability estimation), Wespeaker (speaker similarity for role-play tasks), F5-TTS / ChatTTS / Dia-1.6B (speech synthesis), Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct (text rewriting for TTS preprocessing)
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset and evaluation code will be publicly released under an MIT license. The authors bear all responsibility in case of violation of rights. A data governance process for auditing and removal is maintained, with the right to update assets if consent or licensing concerns arise.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The benchmark includes role-play voice imitation and speaker similarity evaluation involving voice/speaker identity. 100 distinct roles are included with associated audio clips. Five Chinese roles are included among the 100 roles.
rai:dataSocialImpact: VoiceAssistant-Eval is intended to push the boundaries of AI assistant capabilities and guide development of next-generation multimodal models. The benchmark addresses real-world use cases in healthcare, education, smart homes, customer service, and automotive industry. The role-play voice imitation component raises concerns about identity spoofing, harassment, and fraud. Safeguards include: prohibiting training or releasing models intended to reproduce identifiable speakers without documented consent; requiring downstream users to implement consent gating and watermarking; providing safety cards describing acceptable use, known risks, and red-team tests for voice cloning abuse.
rai:dataBiases: The benchmark has a monolingual focus (primarily English, with only five Chinese roles), which may not capture the full variability of real user interactions and may not generalize to diverse linguistic settings. The role-play subset uses a fixed set of 100 roles and associated style prompts, which may encode stereotypes or omit important user personas. Questions and contexts are drawn from academic or synthetic sources, which might not reflect the full richness or fairness concerns of real deployments.
rai:dataLimitations: The dataset (10.5K items) may be limited in diversity. All prompts and evaluations except five Chinese roles are in English. The range of models evaluated is limited, with only one proprietary system (GPT-4o-Audio) included. Evaluation relies on automated measures and GPT-based scoring, which may introduce noise and bias. The benchmark evaluates models in an offline, static manner and does not measure reaction time, handling of partial utterances, barge-in, or error recovery. Video-audio integration and continuous audio-visual streaming tasks are beyond scope. The benchmark may overestimate model capabilities in controlled settings compared to real-world messy input.
rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended for Testing and Evaluation of voice AI assistants and multimodal models. Specific use cases include: evaluating listening ability (natural sounds, music, speech understanding), speaking ability (assistant tasks, emotion, instruction following, multi-round dialogue, reasoning, robustness, role-play, safety), and viewing ability (multi-discipline visual-audio integration). The dataset is not supposed to be used for training models for cheating. Researchers are encouraged to use it to better evaluate voice assistants and facilitate future studies.
